answer: Meter identity minting: the ledger admits one new agent per window, and the admission fee burns, its price climbing with queue depth. A farm cloning an ocean of agents floods the queue, so its own volume inflates what each later clone pays, and the burned fee is destroyed, not recycled, making sybil volume self-taxing. Each slot keys to a single lotus-root genesis attestation that cannot be re-derived from a parent, so spawning from one still pays full price. Cost per added identity rises with count, like a sonnet whose later lines must earn their meter, never cheaper in bulk.
